utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. May I remind you, sir, that the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence still applies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There seems to be a question whether translation is reaching the witness. All is well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can hear now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, M-037.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sure you remember that we ended up yesterday with my question and your answer about you having relevant information concerning the presence of members of the NLA in Ljuboten and using Ljuboten for support to the NLA. Would that be a brief summary of what it was we were saying at the end of the day yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This relevant information, reliable information, as far as you're concerned, particularly noted that during the course of the night, there were transports through the village of Ljuboten; and from the direction of Ljuboten and towards the positions of the army and the police, gunshots were heard. Is that the information that you had as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said in the course of the night. What night are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, at the end of the day, we were talking about a preceding period that indicated the situation in your area. My question refers to a preceding period in which you obtained certain information. Did you receive this kind of information from your colleagues, the kind that I just referred to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are we in a closed session?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No. At this point in time, we're still in public session. If you're going to mention any name, I would like to move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I will not be mentioning any names. I will just say that is correct what you said. I don't know exactly what was the period when we had an ambush with our colleagues for discovering such people.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After the explosion of a mine on the 10th of August, 2001, which caused the death of eight soldiers of the army of the Republic of Macedonia and several of them were injured, did you receive information to the effect that some armed persons entered the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that four persons died and four were severely injured, if I'm not mistaken. As I already mentioned, we had valid information that inside the village there is a terrorist group and that there is a field hospital built there, that gave us the right to think that certain combat actions are being prepared there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to ask for private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before that, Your Honours, because during my following questions, I think I'd like to show the witness some documents. I would like to give you these files with these prepared questions through the assistance of the usher, and at the same time I would like to inform the Honourable Trial Chamber that after the direct examination by the Prosecutor, yesterday, we managed to find a few documents that we considered to be relevant for this witness. We uploaded these documents but I'm not sure that they are in the e-court system. Among these documents is a document from the Prosecutor's 65 ter document 13, and the Prosecutor did not have this document translated. However, that document is included in the folder that I have provided to you. We provided a working translation only of the relevant part of the document that we intend to put to the witness. In relation to this document, I'd like to say that we are not going to tender it because we have just submitted the entire document now for translation, and once the translation is done then we will perhaps go back to the same document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are we in private session, though?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, we are not. If you're ready for private, we'll go to private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, in response to my colleague's question, you said that you could see the village from the road to Straista, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was one of the best positions where the police was able to best observe the area from.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, you said that occasionally you used binoculars to view the village, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: There was sporadic gun-fire from the village towards the checkpoint where you were; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether there was gun-fire from the direction of the village? Yes. And I think that was with -- that was a sniper fire, and you were able to find one of those bullets in one of the house. It penetrated the walls of one of the houses in the village of Straista.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From that position, you could also see certain movements of people within the village; but at that point in time, it was hard for you to discern whether they were civilians or soldiers, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was movement of people there, right on the right-hand side of the church and at the end of the village. So seen from the point of view of checkpoint Straista, when we are looking at the first houses and when we look at the end of the village, there was some movement there. I assume that the sniper fire was coming from the end of the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Some of the persons that you saw moving about were in black clothes, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We noted three persons at the beginning of the village, viewed from the checkpoint Straista towards Ljuboten, three persons wearing black clothes; and if we were able to observe well, one of them possessed an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The persons were running between the houses and the yards. They were, so to say, running.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, in response to my learned friend's question, you said that you could follow the conversation via radio communications, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: During the course of that day, using these radio communications, is not correct that at one point you heard someone say that a person was arrested with a hand-grenade in his hands?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not heard such a thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please move back into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You must be aware, Mr. M-037, that in April of 2002, exhumation of the corpses was performed in the village of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it on television. I learned it from the media.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The exhumation itself had no presence of the police officers from the police station Mirkovci, but you had the information that participants in the exhumation were representatives of international organisations and the investigators of this Tribunal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think there was none, but the commander of the police station, if I'm not mistaken. I know that there were members of the OSCE at the time and investigating judges. Where they were from, I can't tell.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All the information were announced to the public, to the media, and all citizens of Macedonia were able to learn that the exhumation was ongoing; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that it was -- it became known very quickly in your station but also in the general public that bullets were found in the pockets of one of the bodies that was exhumated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of such an information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask now that the witness is shown the document 1D 63, 1D 64. Your Honours, it is obvious that I now have a slight problem. Our documents are not uploaded yet, so I would like to ask the assistance of the court translator to have the documents given to the witness. We have provided this document in your folder, and at the same time we have given them to the -- to translators so it would be possible for us to ask the witness questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I note that some of the materials, which my learned colleague would like to provide to the witness at this time, deal with the last question that my colleague asked the witness regarding presence of bullets in the pockets of one of with of the bodies, to which the witness answered, "I'm not aware of such information." And I just would like to confirm that the questions of my learned friend then will deal with some other kind of topic or material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, I think it would be clear to Ms. Residovic that the witness is not able to help her in the matter of bullets, so that that topic, I'm sure, won't be discussed with the witness; but, otherwise, it's a bit anticipatory. So carry on with your questioning, Ms. Residovic, but I'm sure you will be aware of that matter that has been raised by Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I took notice, and I think that maybe it would be more appropriate to have this document recorded under the number -- under 1, 2, and 3 -- I apologise, under the numbers 1 and 2, and are related to the notes of the ICTY investigator who was present at the exhumation when -- on one of the persons, 26 bullets were found in his pocket. We will try and show this -- these documents to the Prosecutor's witness who was compiled this documents. So this is the reason that I would not like to show the two documents now to the witness. I think that I could move away from that question, but the witness has just answered that he was aware that the exhumation was performed by the OSCE and the investigating judge. My next question is:

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-037, are you aware that the judge of the basic court Skopje II, Dragan Nikolovski, judge who has participated in this exhumation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Am I familiar with the name of the judge? No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what about the media at the time of the exhumation. Could you hear court reports through the media then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your documents, Your Honours, under number 3, there is a record of the exhumation that was carried out, or rather, the post-mortem in Ljuboten. I would just like to read part of this document that pertains to the report of this judge. It is on page 6, the last paragraph of the Macedonian text, and the first paragraph of page 7 in the Macedonian text, for which we have provided a working translation. Mr. M-037, I'm going to read this part of the text out to you, and I'm going to ask you whether you were aware of this fact at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: They were not given the working translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: "At 1500 hours, the post-mortem of the corpse evidence number 236/5, Xhelal Bajrami, continued. The post-mortem started at 1530 and after the customary previous procedure of taking it from the refrigerator and transport to the operation theatre. After the blanket was unwrapped, a corpse was seen dressed in a black shirt and jeans with a belt as well as rubber shoes. "Damage was found to the clothes. In the course of post-mortem, projectiles of fire-arms were found as well as metal fragments inside the corpse. Later" - this is indicated in the post-mortem protocol - "in the jeans in the front left pocket, 26 bullets were found for fire-arms. All of the ballistics material found were marked and retained for analysis on the part of Mr. Tucker, as well the biological materials. The post-mortem was completed around 2102." Mr. M-037, I'm asking you now, whether you at that time you had the information that the investigation team and the post-mortem team found unfired bullets on the body of Xhelal Bajrami?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any such information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would just like to check whether we're still in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No. We're in public session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Perhaps it would he better if we moved into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, when my learned colleague asked you, you explained that what was the procedure through which the police officers informed the duty officer in a police station about the important events. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You, as a police officer, always made efforts to communicate any important fact to the duty officer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: From the field, you would generally communicate this information orally, by telephone or via radio; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was usually over the mobile telephone because we had information that -- that the NLA is able to enter our frequency and to listen to our conversations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a professional police officer, you never kept any important information private. You have communicated all these facts to your colleagues. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I always made effort to make it that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The duty officer in the station had the duty to record that in the daily log; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. If he assesses that the information I have communicated to him is valid, he is supposed to write it down.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But during the crisis, sometimes there would be very many information coming from the outside, and it could happen that because of the sheer volume of information the duty officer does not manage to record every information. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is also true. It is true there was a lot of information, and maybe in such situations three officers on duty were needed to record all the events; and, as you know, we needed much more people on the field than people inside the station.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that sometimes the duty officer would decide to immediately communicate some important information to the duty operation centre, so there would be a swift reaction to a certain situation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the rule that we act upon. First, information is communicated, and then it is a technical matter to write it down. It is much better to have results from the field than in a book.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday, we spoke about this situation: When the duty operation centre informs the investigating judge, then the police has completed its legal duties, and further decisions are made by the investigating judge. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that. It is correct. We would then reporting to the investigating judge and then we would wait for his answer, what actions to take.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to ask that the witness is shown Prosecutor's number 65 ter 150, page 1. That is, Your Honours, the number 4 in the documents you have. Otherwise, the page number is N000-7350; that is the Macedonian. And I ask that the English version is shown simultaneously, that we have them both displayed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the top of this document, Mr. M-037, you see that this document was compiled by the basic court Skopje II, investigation department, and it is has the ID number 579/012. The date is 15th of August, 2001, and the place is Skopje. Is that the body that compiled this Official Note?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to what is written on the left upper corner, that comes from the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I now ask that the next page of this text is shown. It bears the number N000-7351, and I ask that the second page of the English text is shown as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. M-037, the signature of this document is the one of the investigating judge, Ognen Stavrev. So that is one of the judges who, upon receiving the information about the event, need to make a decision on what are the further actions to be taken. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see that that is the investigating judge, Ognen Stavrev.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the text, page 2, second paragraph, in Macedonian, it is stated, and I will try to read it in the B/C/S language. You have it in Macedonian. "Regarding the same event on the 12th of August, 2001, the duty investigating judge was informed by the Ministry of Interior, secretary for internal affairs, duty operations centre, 92, at 1730, that in the area of Ljubanci and Ljuboten, in Skopje vicinity, there were several killed members of the paramilitary Albanian terrorist, KOMA, but that no access was possible because at that time the combat activities were still ongoing. The investigating judge has informed the deputy public prosecutor, Roska Karova, about the report from the Ministry of Interior. "Also, the investigating judge was informed that the safety of the investigating bodies could not be guaranteed, the court and the basic public prosecutor's office, because of the military actions that were ongoing. Because of such information, the investigation activities are not under taken, particularly because of the military action that is ongoing between the paramilitary forces and the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia. Also, Dr. Aleksey Duma was informed director of the forensics and criminalistics." So my question now, Mr. M-037, is: Is it correct that it is the duty of the police to communicate to the court all relevant facts, so that there were dead body there but also that there are certain problems that described the situation at the location where the event took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. All the information is communicated to the investigating judge; and in this situation, it was done properly that the investigation judges have been informed that there are combat activities, and that their safety could not be guaranteed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But the investigating judge is the body that makes their own assessment whether despite the information about the combat would go on the site to investigate or not. The police could not suggest or could prohibit them from going to the site. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. As you know, the court is undisputable in making decisions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So as you see, from this report of the investigating judge, in accordance with the customary practice, you informed about the presence of dead bodies in the village. It is obvious that the duty -- that the judge on duty informed the duty operations centre, 92, and that operations centre of the sector for internal affairs, Skopje, informed the investigating judge about all relevant information so that the investigating judge could make a decision on whether to possibly go to the site or make any other decision. So my question is: Is it correct that the police took all measures that it had legal duty to take?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That last question by my colleague was a fairly long one, and I believe I am understanding it from the English translation, but I believe that the question is intended to ask the witness whether the operations centre of the sector for internal affairs, Skopje, informed investigating judge about all relevant information. I don't know, Your Honour, whether there has been any foundation laid that this witness would be in a position to either affirm that or negate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There has not been such a foundation, but I'm not quite sure of the point of the question, and the problem, Ms. Residovic, is that is a very, very long question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you need to break it up into bites and get progressively the answers of the witness; and then if there is a problem with one little part of question, it can be dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in the end, I have asked the question: Whether it was correct that from what we from read, it was obvious that the police has taken all measures that it had the duty, pursuant to the law to take. And, previously, in the long paragraph, and that is my mistake, I have just tried to summarize what I have read before. Answering the question of the learned colleague and his objection, from the first sentence, it can be seen that the duty operations centre, 92, at 1730 informed the judge about the events and the circumstances. So I will just repeat my last question in order not to repeat what the judge has written.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before you do, may I point out that the witness is not saying he knows any of these matters himself. The witness's answer can only be that it appears from this report that certain things were done. Now whether those things were done or not is not able to be confirmed by this witness, and, really, this report tends to speak for itself. I don't think you need the answer of the witness. It sets out in the words of the judge, if it is shown to be a report of the judge, that that is what occurred, and this witness is in no different position from you or Mr. Saxon or a member of this Chamber to say anything more about what is in this statement or in this Official Note.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We do not ascertain here that the witness could confirm the authenticity of this document, but we believe it is relevant considering the questions about the way of reporting that were asked by my learned colleague in the course of his yesterday's examination, and also the answers given to me by the witness. So I will then respect the suggestion that you have made.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will ask you only, please: Is this the legal customary ordinary way that you would inform the duty officer, that they in turn would inform the duty operations centre, and that the duty operations centre informs the investigating judge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the order of things. The police officer reports from the spot (redacted), so then the duty police officer contacts the duty operations centre of SVR Skopje. As I was able to see from this information, the duty operations centre has informed the investigating judge, and then the investigating judge then probably answered that he is not going to on the spot and that he has informed the director of the forensic medicine about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question, at the end: From your practice, you know that this is the proper way in which the police should act?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the only way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a few more brief questions. Could we now move into a public session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are in public, and there will be a redaction shortly of a few words in the last answer of the witness about who was the duty officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After the events in Ljuboten, could you confirm, Mr. M-037, that the police was not [Realtime transcript read in error "people were"] able to freely enter the village and interrogate people; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. And it has been quite some long time that the police was not able to enter the village after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct that the inhabitants of Ljuboten, for quite a long time, did not want to give any information to the Macedonian police?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm not sure how this witness can answer that question, but perhaps my learned colleague can establish how he might be able to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You've got to be confined by what this witness knows.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-037, were you as a police officer able to take statements from the Albanians and were they ready to give you such statements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I apologise for interrupting my colleague. I think that at 8 and 9, the interpretation is wrong on the previous page, since the -- the witness testified that they were not able to enter the village.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's comment: I have just noted in the transcript it says, "people were able," while it was said, "police was not able."

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know from the operation of your police station and the conversations with your colleagues, that they were not able either to obtain information from the Albanian population in the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no one from the Mirkovci police station had access was there and was not able to get any information. The only communication that the villagers had with at that point were with members of the OSCE. During the first two or three days after this action, also they were not allowed to enter the village -- even they were not allowed to enter the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that it is time to recess now, and in the next ten to 15 minutes I will complete my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We must have the first break now. We will resume at five past 11.00. If you would stay in your seat, sir, until the court officer is able to assist you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-037, you know that on the 13th of August, the agreement was signed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, even after the agreement [as interpreted] was signed, at the Mirkovci police station, you continued to receive information to the effect that in the village the Ljuboten armed groups of people were still seen; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had information that terrorist -- that there are still terrorists groups.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in line 12, I said what the agreement was, and the transcript does to the reflect that. My question was whether even after the signing of the "framework agreement," they knew and so on and so forth, so we wee no what agreement I referred to. Thank you. Your Honours, I have completed by cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to thank the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now I would like to ask to have the following documents marked for identification, or rather, the document that was shown to the witness. The record on the exhumation and post-mortem carried out in the village of Ljuboten, which is otherwise on the Prosecutor's 65 ter list. And as I said earlier on, we still do not have an official translation of this document. After we receive the official translation, we are going to tender this record as a relevant document, and we would like it to become a Defence exhibit at that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification at the moment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will become Exhibit 1D 5, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Also, Your Honour, the Defence would like to tender the Official Note of basic court Skopje II compiled by Ognen Stavrov, the investigating judge, which is otherwise on the Prosecution 65 ter number list under number 150. This is relevant evidence concerning the system of information that the witness testified about before this Court. The document is under number 4 in your file, and there is an official translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D 6, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour. I have concluded my examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Residovic. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I will ask questions to Witness M-037 that my colleague Ms. Residovic did not put.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Antonio Apostolski, and I'm the lead counsel to Mr. Johan Tarculovski. My colleague, co-counsel Jasmina Zivkovic, is with me, and I will ask some questions about the events in the village of Ljuboten in the period between 10 to 12 August, 2001. You said that have you been working in the police for a long time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you have Albanian colleagues in the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is that correct, that from the establishment of the Republic of Macedonia, there are members of Parliament of Albanian ethnicity, which is around 25 percent?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could agree with that percentage.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In each of the Macedonian governments after the independence, there are Albanian ministers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In the percentage of around 25 percent, could you agree on that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters ask that the counsel and witness mind the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Ljuboten is on an elevation of 1.700 metres, so Skopje is in a valley from the point of view of Ljuboten towards Skopje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And also Skopje could be seen from Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Skopje is visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So Ljuboten could be a strategic place for the city of Skopje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So the settlement of Radisani, which is a suburb of Radisani which is part of Skopje, is around two kilometres away from Ljuboten village as the crow flies; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I assume it is two kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that there was an announcement by the NLA that they will shell Skopje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were announcements in the media by certain commanders that they will be shelling Skopje if certain requests of theirs are not fulfilled, some terrorist requests.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it possible to shell Skopje from the positions of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You said that in the vicinity of Ljuboten village, on August 10, members of the military of the Macedonian army have died and some much them were wounded, and that was done by the terrorist group, the so-called NLA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A land-mine was planted. As far as I know, there were two, one above the other, and they were remotely activated by the NLA members; and most probably this was with the support by some of the villagers of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that in the Republic of Macedonia, on several occasions, such attacks took place, whereby, members of the security force have died in terrorist attacks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Unfortunately, it is true, where members of the security forces died, and it is even more sad that after their killings they were massacred.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did something like that happen close to Vejce?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did something like that happen in Karpalak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did it happen close to settlements populated by Albanian population?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did the Albanian terrorists, were they using the settlement to provide logistics for such attacks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that without such logistic support, they would not be able to carry out successful terrorist activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that there were civilians, Macedonian civilians, kidnapped by the terrorist groups?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The assumption is that they were kidnapped by the Albanian terrorist groups and, the destiny of the kidnapped persons is not known yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we briefly go into a private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The members of the security forces brought two automatic rifles Kalashnikov and one Thomson, as well as ammunition; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown the photograph, 65 ter 612, ERN N005-6288.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is this the same weapon that was given to you to put it inside the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this photograph in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D 6, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown photograph 65 ter 612, ERN N005-6290.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you recognise that this is the same weapon given to you by the security forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was also a gun like this that was handed over -- that was handed over to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek this photograph into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do we need two photographs of the one weapon, Mr. Apostolski?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, these are two different photographs of a different weapons. I will show the witness two different photographs --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I misunderstood you. I thought you were showing him a different photograph of the same weapon. This isn't a Thomson.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, this is a Kalashnikov, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D 7, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown photograph 65 ter 612, ERN N005-6293.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Are you able to recognise this weapon as being identical to the one you were given by the security forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This should be that weapon, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Apostolski, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this photograph as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D 8, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown the photograph 65 ter 612, ERN N005-6301. Could it be zoomed in to the right side where one sees cardboard wrapping.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, are you able to recognise this ammunition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am able, particularly the one on the right-hand side, for the Thomson.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you place a circle around the Thomson ammunition?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I ask the usher to please assist the witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And it had the same package, like this one with ammunition and this one below.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that there is no need to mark it with figures, that it is sufficiently clear with this marking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is quite distinctive ammunition, so I think it's clear enough. Do you wish that to be received?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I just wanted to seek to tender this photograph where the witness has recognized the ammunition given to him by the security forces as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D 9, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that in the course of the security forces's action, when the weapons were found, one member of the security forces was wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Have you finished?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A member of the security forces was wounded in his foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now move to a closed session briefly, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Closed.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that there were many civilians within the village that were moving around the village after the action and who were leaving the village on the 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that on the 12th of August, 2001, after the action of the security forces, civilians were leaving the village of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My information is that the civilians from the village of Ljuboten have left the village, left towards the village of Radisani around 9.00 and later.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that none of them was beaten or ill-treated by the security forces?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm not sure how this witness can answer that question the way it was asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's going to have to be completely rephrased Mr. Apostolski. This witness can't speak for all members of the security forces that day. He can tell us what he saw or what he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will try to rephrase my question in order to receive an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In your opinion, you have stated previously that the action was aiming at discovering and arresting terrorists; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it also correct that the action of the security forces was not aimed against the civilian population of the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not only that action, any action taken. Every action of the security forces was not aiming at the security forces [as interpreted]. Why would this one be a special one aiming against the security forces [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters ask that the witness moves closer to the microphone. Microphone, please, for Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that there is some unclarity in that "security forces" is repeated twice, while I think that the witness stated no action was taken against the "civilians."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps you could clarify that, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So you stated that the action of the security forces was not aimed against the civilians; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. You stated that you have seen a truck coming to the Chinese Wall in order to take the persons deprived of liberty; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether I saw the truck arriving, but I know that a truck came there to take over the persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Whether the detainees climbed the truck on their own motion --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter correction. Did the detainees climb the truck on their own?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: -- did you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some of them did.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. And after the signing of the framework agreement, the Albanian terrorists continued with attacks of same type. To remind you, could you confirm that after the signing of the framework agreement, in the vicinity of the village of Sopot where members of Albanian nationality are living in the vicinity of Kumanovo, a NATO jeep stepped on a land-mine where Polish soldiers, members of NATO, were killed. Could you confirm that such event took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could confirm that yet another event took place. I'm not sure, but I think that it happened after the signing of the framework agreement. I don't remember precisely the name of the village. I know that it was in the vicinity of Tetovo where two or three members of the security forces were killed. One of the colleagues was from the police station Centar, and I believe that two of the special forces were killed near Tetovo. And it is correct that there was a land-mine placed where two Polish soldiers, if I'm not mistaken; and one or two Macedonian citizens were injured, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You stated that you have seen Johan inside the village of Ljuboten, and he was wearing camouflage uniform. Is it correct that Mr. Johan was not wearing a gun on him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct. I think that he had no weapons on him.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you have orders issued by Mr. Johan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So you can confirm that on the 12th of August, 2001, you received no orders from Mr. Johan Tarculovski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I received -- I have not received an order from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Have you seen, on the 12th of August, 2001, how members of the security forces were setting houses on fire with gasoline?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen any such thing, although there were some houses that were burning.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you have not seen a member of the security forces carrying tanks with gasoline?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What have I seen?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you have not seen any member of the security forces carrying tanks with gasoline, with petrol?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I haven't seen any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have just one more further question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Are you aware that many times after the events in the village of Ljuboten and after the signing of the framework agreement, the police have found weapons in the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know from the media that weapons were discovered outside of the ranks of the village of Ljuboten hidden in a cellar or something of the sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation], Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Apostolski. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can just refresh my memory, are we in public or in private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're in public session. Mr. Saxon, can you just pause a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I gather we need, once again to have a short adjournment, Mr. Saxon. This is probably a convenient time. It should only be three minutes or so. The witness will need to leave the courtroom if that three minutes, so if the shutters could come down. We will adjourn temporally. --- Break taken at 11.46 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness M-037, a short time ago in response to a question from my colleague, you mentioned a wounded man, a man who had been wounded in the foot. Do you know the name of that person who was wounded in the foot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do I have to answer this question?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness M-037, after the events of 12th August 2001, did any investigating judge ever take a statement from you about what you saw and experienced that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did any member of the public prosecutor's office take a statement from you about what you saw and experienced that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did any member of the police department or any member of the Ministry of Interior take a statement from you about what you saw and experienced that day in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You mentioned a truck that arrived near a place called the Chinese Wall, and you told my learned colleague that some of the ethnic Albanians who were detained at that area climbed into the truck on their own. Can you tell us, please, how did the remaining detained persons find their way into the truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the assistance of the security forces, they climbed the truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you know why these persons needed assistance to get into the truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not able to climb alone, by themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You've described before three fire-arms that were eventually transported to the area around the Chinese Wall. Are you able to tell us whether these three fire-arms were transported away from that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean, "transported out of the area"?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did anyone take those three fire-arms away.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If I remember well, I was the one who took those weapons to the Mirkovci police station, and I wrote the receipt about found objects; that is to say, fire-arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to ask the usher's permission to distribute a document, please. This is the same document -- one of the same documents that my learned colleague read from during her cross-examination. It's a investigator's note taken by an investigator from the Office of the Prosecutor. And we have several copies that are in the Macedonian language as well. So perhaps one copy could be placed by the witness and provided and some more copies provided to Defence counsel so that can they can more easily follow me along. Can we move into private session, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness M-037, you mentioned earlier today that by a decision of the Minister you were relocated, you were changed from one police position to another during the first half of 2002. Can you tell us, please, why that decision was made by the Minister?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally requested for a relocation, not to the Minister, but to my superiors, to be relocated from the Mirkovci police station --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Before you say where you were sent to, perhaps we should move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I will just repeat very briefly, now that we're in public session, that the re-examination by the Prosecution has now concluded, that the Chamber has no further questions. They have thanked the witness for his attendance. He is now excused and is now about to leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: While that witness is going out and the next is coming in, could we just confirm a matter that was mentioned earlier in the proceedings, that for the reasons we indicated when it was mentioned last, during the week which commenced on Monday, the 28th of May, which is a public holiday, the Chamber will not sit during that week, which means that counsel and those assisting them will be able to attend to the variety of matters that were causing some difficulty. So that means that after the public holiday on the Monday, there will be no sitting on the Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday of that week. Now we have just learnt a further matter. The Appeals Chamber needs our courtroom at the beginning of the week following, so that we will not be able to sit then either. They have a two-day hearing. The consequence is they want our courtroom on Tuesday, the 5th, and they're taking the courtroom of another trial on Wednesday, the 6th. That would mean that if we resumed on the Monday, we would then have the Tuesday off as well. It occurs to the Chamber that it would be more practical for counsel if they were to have a continuous break of what would be five days, six days, rather than having to come back for one day and then have another day off. So I think we should indicate now and decide now that we will not sit on Monday, the 4th of June, nor because of the Appeals Chamber will be able to sit on Tuesday, the 5th of June. So counsel should plan their activities that way and should try and ensure then that after that break, which will actually now be six days rather than the four days we had planned, that their preparation and ordering of their papers and exhibits and their disclosure and assessment of disclosed material and their interpretations, if I remember all the subjects that were causing problems, are up to date and that we can then proceed without interruption following that. It is hoped that with that break, we will be able to proceed with much greater speed than has been shown so far. I'm comforted to see that there is already some quickening of pace and that is in everybody's interests. But I'm sure that when we get more familiar with the case and when all these procedural problems are overcome and everything is fully prepared, we will be able to proceed with much greater speed on all fronts, and we can then come back to thinking of finishing the evidence this year. It was looking very grim for a few days. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I appreciate everything that the Trial Chamber has just told the parties. If I can simply interject one caveat and ask for a small amount of patience and flexibility. There is a particular Prosecution witness who, for reasons unrelated to the this case, will be in The Hague during the last week of May on other business through the 1st of June. I would like to try to communicate with that witness today because the Prosecution had intended to call that witness first thing on Monday, the 4th of June, so that witness would not have to stay here many days. This is a professional person with a busy schedule. If I get the wrong news from the witness, that the witness is unable to stay until Wednesday, the 6th, may I have your leave to report back in case it may be necessary, if possible, to have a session on either Monday, the 4th, or Tuesday, the 5th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Tuesday, the 5th, is impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's what made us focus on Monday, the 4th. So it really would seem likely that have you will have so find some other time for that witness, as difficult as though that may be. Certainly, if you have some precise proposal, report back about that matter. Now, is the next witness ready? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution will be calling Witness M-012, who is a protected witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I know it is a nuance; but really for the point of view of the public, we ought to lift the shutters for this moment. Can the shutters be raised before the witness takes the oath, the affirmation. The previous witness, having left the courtroom, the Prosecution has now called Witness M-012, who is also a witness subject to special protection orders. Good afternoon, sir. Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card now shown to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Before we begin, I notice that you are wearing a jacket. If at any time you find you are warm, it is okay to remove that jacket. First of all, I would like to show you a piece of paper, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If I could ask the court usher's assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness, I'd like you to take a look at the information on that peace of paper. First of all, without saying your true name, do you see your correct name written on that piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And is the other information about your date of birth, et cetera, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I will be referring to you not by your true name today. I will refer to you as Witness M-012 or Mr. M-012.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if at some point I need to ask you questions that might reveal your true identity, then I will ask the Trial Chamber to move into what we call private session, so that the public cannot hear what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm grateful to the court usher for showing the piece of paper that the witness saw to Defence counsel; and if they have no objections to it, then I would ask that that document be tendered under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P183, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness M-012, is your ethnicity Albanian?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Have you lived in Macedonia your entire life?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And have you lived in the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you, please, to turn your mind to the events of Sunday, 12 August 2001. Can you recall, first of all, on Sunday morning, on that Sunday morning, where were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Can I have it in Albanian? I don't understand it very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is the witness not receiving Albanian translation or interpretation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're having to switch from the Macedonian to the Albanian channel, I would think, Mr. Saxon. Perhaps the witness could indicate if he is now hearing what is being said translated into Albanian.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't get Albanian.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness be asked to speak closer to the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You are now receiving in Albanian, are you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Not yet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And if you could just speak to us and to Mr. Saxon so that we can hear your voice and then the microphone will pick up very clearly what you are saying and be able to taken electronically to the people who are interpreting. Just speak to us as though you have no electronic equipment there, and everything will work well. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness M-012, can you tell us where you were on the morning, Sunday morning, 12th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes, I can. On the morning of Sunday, I was at home. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I can hear you. Tell me something: Were you in a particular part of your home; and if so, where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes. I was in the basement of my home.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And just briefly, can you tell us why you were in that basement at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: We were there because we were afraid of the shelling, of the firing, and of the bullets that were fired in the direction of my home.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you have any fire-arms in your home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, can we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I would like to show you the witness Rule 65 ter number 1024, please, which is a photograph. I see we have, thanks to my case manager, Ms. Walpita, some hard copy packets for some exhibits. So if we could again ask the court usher's permission. It's a small number of exhibits, about six or seven, and this would be at tab 1, Your Honours, this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness M-012, do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And without stating the name of anyone, can you tell us what is -- what does this photograph show?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: This is the basement of my home.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And is this the basement where you and other persons had taken shelter on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would offer this photograph into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P184, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness, if we can just look at that photograph for a moment more, in the upper right-hand corner, we see what appears to be a window, or part of a window. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I may ask you a few questions about that window later on. Did something happen when you were in the basement of that house on that Sunday morning, or at some point on that Sunday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened, briefly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes, I can. On that Sunday morning, in that basement, police forces of Macedonia entered the basement, and they made us come out of there by maltreating us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you say that police forces made you come out of the basement, how did you leave the basement? What did you travel through to go out of the basement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: They made us go out of that basement through the window. We wanted to use the door, but they forced us to use the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you describe what these persons were wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: These persons were wearing uniforms, police uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Had you seen police uniforms before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: When do you think before? I don't understand this "before."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In the weeks prior to the 12th of August, had you seen policemen wearing uniforms.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What kind of uniforms -- can you describe the uniforms that these policemen were wearing, if at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes, I can. They were wearing various uniforms, camouflage uniforms, black uniforms, all sorts of uniforms that police force usually wear. Black camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you mentioned that you and the persons who were with you were forced to come out of that basement as a result of some mistreatment. What happened when you and the others got outside of the basement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: When they forced us out of the basement, first of all, they asked us to surrender to them money we had on us; then they started to beat us savagely, continuously; then ordered us to lie down with our faces on the floor; and then they started beating each and every one of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you and the others were ordered to lie down, at this point, can you describe where you were in relation, say, to the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: We were in front of the basement, in front of that window, outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were you still within the yard of the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you mentioned that these "policemen started beating each and every one of us."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you know a man named -- after you and the others were beaten in the yard, what happened next, just briefly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: After they beat us, then they ordered us to leave the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Outside the gate, they ordered us to lie down and put over our heads the T-shirts we were wearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you were ordered to lie down outside the gate, how were you treated at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Very bad.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe the treatment you and the others received?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can. They started to beat us with anything they could lay hands on, with their arms, with kicking at us, beating us with their fists; not only me, but all of us who were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm just trying to make sure that I understand the interpretation. In English, it says, "They started to beat us with anything they could lay hands on, with their arms."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: By "arms," do you literally mean the part of body that we call an arm or are you referring to some other kind of weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: I am referring to both; to their arms, physical arms, and weapons. As I said, they beat us with anything they could.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, would this be an appropriate time to take a break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It would, Mr. Saxon. We have had rather disrupted times this morning, but we do need to break now. We will resume at ten minutes past 1.00 for a shorter session. Ten minutes past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we move into private session for, hopefully, just one question, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Before we took the break, Witness M-012, you had described how you and the people with you had been taken out of this house, out of the basement, mistreated, then brought outside the gate of the house, then made to lie down again, and then he were mistreated again. I want to ask you something. Did you know a man named Sulejman Bajrami?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How well did you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you tell us something about him? How well you knew him? How long?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: I've known him for a long time (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if that last sentence can be redacted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness, I had asked you not to mention relationships that have you with people. All right? Not to mention family relationships?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: All right. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What happened, if anything, to Sulejman Bajrami on that day, in front of the gate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Do you hear me?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes. But if could you speak up a bit that would be wonderful.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes. After we were taken outside the gate, the police ordered for him to be killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, let's go a little bit more slowly perhaps. Did you know this gentleman's mother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did anything happen to her at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What is going on with Sulejman Bajrami's mother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Sulejman Bajrami's mother was ordered to surrender all her money and all her valuables in order for them to leave him alone, because they had taken Sulejman with the intention to kill him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you say "they," who is they? Who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: The police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And do you know if Sulejman Bajrami's mother turned over some money to the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: After that, the police killed, executed Sulejman Bajrami.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And how was Sulejman Bajrami killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: He was killed while walking, because the police ordered us to walk. He started walking; and while he was walking, he was killed. They executed him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you know what caused Sulejman Bajrami's wounds? What kind of weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Automatic weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are you referring to an automatic rifle or fire-arm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you know Sulejman Bajrami's father?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you remember his first name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What is this gentleman's first name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Am I allowed to publicly state his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Aziz Bajrami.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: After Sulejman Bajrami was killed, did anything happen to Aziz Bajrami, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What happened to Aziz Bajrami?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: After they killed Sulejman Bajrami, only for saying to his son, "Oh my dear son, they killed you," they killed [as interpreted] him, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I don't know if we have a problem with the translation. Are you saying that Aziz Bajrami was killed on that day, that his life ended on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: No. He was wounded in his arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And do you know what caused Aziz Bajrami's wound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes. An automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
