utterances.text: Witness M-012, I have to show you a photograph now. It's not a very pretty photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If I could have the court officer's assistance, please, to show 65 ter number 201. It's a photograph bearing the ERN N000-2185.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness M-012, do you see the photograph in front of you on that computer screen, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you tell us what is depicted there in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: The body of Sulejman Bajrami.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If that photograph could be tendered into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P185, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it can be removed out in from the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you know if anyone else in that group of people that was being mistreated in front of the house was killed that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What was the name of the person who was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Muharem Ramadani.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We're going to take about that incident in a moment. Before we do, I want to ask you if you know a man by the name of Ismail Ramadani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to him at that time when the group was being mistreated in front of the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What happened to Ismail Ramadani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: During the mistreatment by the police, he was stabbed on his back. They carved a cross on his back with a knife.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Again, when you use the word "they," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: The police. I refer to the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At some point, did you actually see the injuries to Mr. Ramadani's back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And I don't want to jump ahead too much, but can you tell us just briefly when did you see the injuries to his back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: I saw the injuries on his back when we were at the Mirkovci police station, in the garage there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. We'll come to that in a few minutes. A few minutes ago, you mentioned that Muharem Ramadani died in Ljuboten that day. Do you know -- first of all, let me ask you: How well did you know Muharem Ramadani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And how did you know him? How long had you known him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: From my childhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what do you know about what happened to Muharem Ramadani on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: I know that he was killed by the Macedonian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you actually see that happen, or is this something that you were told about later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: I was told about this later, while in prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I would like to show the witness --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I would like to show the witness another photograph from 65 ter 201. This is tab 3 in your binders, Your Honour. It's a photograph with the ERN N000-2098.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness, do you see this photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you tell us what you see in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And just for the record --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And just to be complete and clear, this is Muharem Ramadani we see here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P186, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I believe a few minutes ago you mentioned that you and the others in the group had to walk somewhere. Where did you have to walk?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. The police ordered us to walk towards the Brace's House; and from there, they told us that they were going to take us to Ljubanci.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very briefly, while you were walking to Brace's House, how were you treated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Very badly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you describe briefly how you were treated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes. They were beating us with automatic rifle-butts. They were cursing us, offending us. They maltreated us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you use the pronoun "they," who is they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: The Macedonian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just heard one of the accused say something. I don't know if the witness heard it, but I hope whatever it was it's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you could have a word with your client, Mr. Apostolski, after the break, at the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, it may actually have been the other accused who made it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, then.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It was me without the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BOSKOSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I can't hear well with the headsets, so maybe I spoke too loud because I wasn't hearing. I will be silent. I will just talk to myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you arrived at the place known as Brace's House, what happened to you there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: There the maltreatment and beating increased.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At some point, did something happen to your clothes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What happened to the clothes that you were wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: They started beating me savagely, hitting me on my body and head, and at that moment I fell somewhere. When I regained consciousness, I noticed that I had no longer my trousers on me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did you also have your underwear on or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you have any item of clothing covering any part of your body at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Just a T-shirt covering my head.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And I must apologise, there was a question I should have asked you much sooner, and let me step back for a moment. Going back to the time when you and the other persons were in the basement of the house, can you recall, approximately, what time these policemen entered, approximately, on that 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: You mean at what time, the hour?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Approximately, what time, yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: About 12.00. I was not wearing a watch, but I think it was about this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Let's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, you're encouraged for technical reasons to have a little longer break between the end of the witness's answer and the commencement of your question; and if the witness could try to do the same. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What was your condition like when you realised that at least from the waist down you had no clothes on? What was your condition like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: I was in a very difficult position.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you be a little bit more precise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes. I was very tired. I was covered in blood. My face, my body were covered in blood. I can't describe it in words. I was in a very bad condition.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And after a while then, after a while at the area called the Brace's House, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: After the beating and the maltreatment, they made us get on a truck in order to take us to a destination that they wanted us to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, again, when you say "they," who is they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: The Macedonian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And do you know where you were taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Where were you taken then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: They took us to the Mirkovci police station. Before we reached this police station, they stopped at Ljubanci village.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you say "us," are you referring to the people who were in that basement with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you got to the Mirkovci police station, what part of the Mirkovci police station were you taken to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: In a garage.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And was the entire -- was this entire group of people then taken to the garage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How were you treated inside that garage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Very badly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe how you were treated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes. They ordered us to lay down on our stomachs, and they started to beat us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you say "they," can you be more precise? Who is "they"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: The Macedonian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you recall what the Macedonian police used to beat you and the others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Everything. Everything they wanted to use.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How many times were you beaten in that garage, if you can recall, or if you can estimate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: We were beaten many times, and I quite don't remember how many times because after the beatings, I would lose consciousness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At some point, were you taken out of that garage for a time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: To a room upstairs, a police room.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What happened inside that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: They interrogated us about things that we were not familiar with.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm just speaking about you right now. Who interrogated you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: The police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, what subjects you were interrogated about. What specifically were you asked about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: They asked me about things about persons whom I didn't know, then they forced me to sign a document. I did not want to sign this document. I wanted them to turn on the lights so that I could see and read the document, but they did not approve my request, and one of them said, "Well, he is still tough enough to endure some more beating," and ordered me to go back downstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And by "downstairs," do you mean back to the garage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: After you returned to the garage, what happened to you there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: The beatings continued.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we move into private session, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At some point, Witness M-012, was there any kind of examination made of your hands at the Mirkovci police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Can you be more clear what you mean by the word "examination."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did someone come and do something with your hands.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber what that was, please. What was done to your hands?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can. They told us that they will make a paraffin glove test.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And were you told what the purpose of that test was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see the hour. Would this be a convenient time for me to pause in my testimony -- excuse me, pause in my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon. We must finish for the day. We resume again tomorrow at 9.00 a.m.. If you would wait where you are, the court officer will show you out afterward. And we must stop now but we will continue tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning, if you could return then. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 16th day of May, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.46 p.m.,
